metric: Real on-display Flutter FrameTiming (GPU build + raster ms) over the 180-frame scripted worst-case scene, captured via integration_test/frame_timing_test.dart -d windows (Debug build) on Windows 11 / x64.
why: The headless paint benchmark rasterizes via the SOFTWARE rasterizer, where Picture.toImageSync (offscreen image creation) is pathologically expensive (~14ms/call) and unrepresentative of GPU. That proxy cannot fairly judge an offscreen-image-caching optimization, so the half-resolution Milky Way change is validated here, on the real GPU, instead.
optimization: Milky Way rendered into a HALF-RESOLUTION offscreen image (quarter pixels, half blur sigma) and bilinear-upscaled; the cache now stores the rasterized image so cache-HITS are free blits instead of re-running the Gaussian blur every drawPicture.
perceptual: Golden perceptual-diff gate PASSES: maxDelta 2-3/255 on <=0.0007% of pixels (limit 0.20%) — visually indistinguishable.
note: Debug build inflates absolute ms; the WITH/WITHOUT delta on the same machine/build is the meaningful result. Raster is exactly where the Milky Way Gaussian blur lives. Both before/after are far under the 16.7ms 60fps budget even in Debug; the win matters most on weaker GPUs / higher resolutions / sustained pan-zoom. Reproduce: from the package, 'flutter create --platforms=windows .', then 'flutter test integration_test/frame_timing_test.dart -d windows', then remove the generated windows/ runner (not committed).
